title: GitHub - qarl/arcade-js: Arcade games translated from their original machine code to JavaScript, validated pixel-exact against MAME. An experiment in using AI agents to port existing software.
excerpt: Arcade games translated from their original machine code to JavaScript, validated pixel-exact against MAME. An experiment in using AI agents to port existing software. - qarl/arcade-js
content_html:
An experiment in using AI agents to port existing software. The disassembly, the translation, the tests and the tooling in this repo were produced by agents. Arcade ROMs are the testbed, chosen for one reason: you can prove whether the port is correct.

Most porting work has no oracle. You rewrite something, it looks right, and "faithful" stays a matter of opinion. An arcade ROM doesn't have that problem — MAME already runs it, so there is a reference implementation emitting exact expected output. Correctness becomes falsifiable and frame-by-frame: did our JavaScript produce the same pixels as the original machine code, or did it not?

Concretely, then: arcade games translated from their original machine code to JavaScript, validated pixel-exact against MAME. Not a re-implementation from observation — the ROM is disassembled and translated instruction by instruction, then checked frame against frame until the pixels match.

That falsifiable translation is the foundation. On top of it the port is made readable — routines are decompiled to idiomatic JavaScript, each still proven memory-equivalent to the translation (a sweep that's complete for The Pit and ongoing for Donkey Kong) — and understood — the game's mechanics grounded by playing it in MAME, not guessed from the code. The same oracle does double duty: a gate that proves the pixels match, and a probe we drive to learn what the game means. The whole method is one page: docs/README.md.

Donkey Kong is the first subject, and it is complete. The Pit (Zilec/Centuri, 1982) is the second, and it was chosen deliberately: no public disassembly of it exists, so there was nothing for a model to have memorized — the agents had to recover it from the raw ROM. That makes it the sharper test of the thesis, and the same falsifiable pixel gate keeps it honest. The repo is structured to host many: multiple CPUs, multiple arcade boards, and multiple game romsets, sharing what they genuinely share.

How the agents were organised — the division of labour, the failure modes we actually hit, and what the tooling had to do about them — is written up in docs/how-the-agents-worked.md.

Status — Donkey Kong: plays. All four boards, natural board-to-board progression, and the level loop all work — finish 100m and it wraps back to 25m at the next level, indefinitely — and the rendering is pixel-validated frame-by-frame against MAME 0.288.

Status — The Pit: in progress. Its whole boot→attract sequence runs and renders pixel-exact against MAME; all 169 of its routines are now rewritten into idiomatic JavaScript (memory-equivalent to the oracle, with memory and routines named from evidence, proposer≠confirmer); and its full mechanics — objective, cast, win/lose — have been mapped by playing it under MAME. End-to-end gameplay pixel-validation is the remaining work.

What's here (and what isn't)

This repo ships our tools, our translation (the JavaScript — our own expression of the ROM's logic), and our understanding — each game's gameplay.md (how it's played, from public research) and mechanisms.md (the code-grounded model of how it works). It does not ship the copyrighted ROM data, nor the gitignored build metadata — dk.asm, coverage.json, blocks.def, unreached.txt under games/dkong/out/ (regenerate locally with make trace). You supply your own ROM; make rom-dkong assembles and sha256-verifies it locally. See games/dkong/rom/README.md.

You still need the ROM — here's why

The translation replaces the ROM's logic, not its contents. A ROM is not only code:

  • Graphics and palette are pure data. gfx1 (8×8 tiles), gfx2 (16×16 sprites) and the colour proms have no code in them at all. Without them there is nothing to draw.
  • The code reads the ROM as data. Donkey Kong's first game-state handler runs ld hl,0x01ba / ldir, copying a table straight out of ROM. So the engine still maps the ROM into the address space and reads from it — our JavaScript is what executes, the ROM is still what it reads.

Which is exactly why the copyright line falls where it does: the JavaScript is our own expression of the logic and it ships; the original data is Nintendo's and it never does.

How we know it's right

If the question is whether agents can port software faithfully, the answer is only worth as much as what could have proven it wrong. These gates are the experiment's instrumentation, and every one of them runs from a clean checkout:

Donkey Kong's game-start intro: MAME on the left, arcade-js on the right, driven by the same input tape and aligned with the pixel gate's own frame offset. Both panels are rendered from the very frames.rgb artifacts the gate diffs — not a screen recording of two windows. Shown at 2× speed; over this 35-second run the largest single-frame difference is 0.17%.

  • Pixel gate. Capture a golden from live MAME 0.288 under a pinned, determinism- controlled command line, run the same input tape through our engine, and diff the frames. Movement 6/6 and bonus-item 9/9 scenarios pass across all four board types. Those scenarios poke the board state to start on a given board, which keeps each one short and deterministic — that's a property of the fixtures, not a limit of the game, which progresses on its own.
  • Decoder cross-check. Our Z80 decoder is checked against z80dasm over the whole ROM: 6051 instruction boundaries, zero disagreements in either direction (make verify).
  • Step audit. Every m.step() target in the translation is verified to land on a real instruction boundary (make stepcheck). The static tracer reaches ~77% of the ROM; targets in the spans it hasn't reached are reported as coverage gaps rather than quietly counted as passes — a green gate says what it actually covered.
  • Several thousand unit tests (npm test), with mutation patches recorded next to the assertions they justify, so a test that cannot fail is visible as such. Each idiomatic rewrite additionally carries a memory-equivalence test against the frozen oracle, with deliberately-broken twins it must catch.
  • State and write diffs. RAM and the hardware write surface are diffed independently of pixels, which separates "the CPU translation is wrong" from "the video model is wrong."

Layout

core/                 game-agnostic engine
  cpu/z80.js          the Z80 processor        (any Z80 game reuses this)
  cpu/test/           unit tests for the CPU core
  audio.js            sample-player abstraction (audio lives ABOVE emulation)
boards/               arcade hardware, named by MAME driver (a "board")
  dkong/              memory map · i8257/watchdog/latches · video/palette/geometry
  dkong/hardware.json the same, as JSON: the single source the shared Python gate
                      tools read via --hardware, instead of hardcoding DK addresses
  dkong/test/         unit tests for the board
games/                one directory per romset (dkong, thepit)
  dkong/
    manifest.js       declares its cpu + board + rom set + inputs + metadata
    translated/       the assembly-JS translation of the ROM (the frozen oracle)
    idiomatic/        readable-JS rewrites, each gated memory-equivalent to the oracle
    audio/            sound-command → sample trigger map
    rom/              gitignored — `make rom-dkong` builds it locally
    tapes/            test input tapes (published)
    test/             unit + integration tests for the translation
    entrypoints.json  disassembly entry points (folded into the trace)
    tools/            per-game gate runners (emit.js · move_suite.py · prize_suite.py)
  thepit/             the second game — same shape; its mechanisms.md maps the game
                      as understood so far (see docs/mechanisms)
web/                  browser front-end: pick a game and play it
tools/                disassembler · tracer · MAME golden capture · pixel/state diff ·
                       gate runner (verdict.sh) — shared, game-agnostic
docs/                 the method: one model (docs/README.md) + a technique guide per move

Tests are colocated with the code they test (core/**/test/, boards/**/test/, games/**/test/ — see npm test's glob), not in a separate top-level test/.

The three layers — CPU, board, game — are independent axes. A game's manifest.js names its CPU (z80) and board (dkong); the machine assembles CPU + board + translated ROM. Frogger, for example, would reuse core/cpu/z80.js on a future boards/galaxian/. A board is named for the MAME machine config it implements — usually identical to the driver file (dkong), but not always: The Pit runs the thepit config inside MAME's taito/roundup.cpp family file, so it lives at boards/thepit/ while its hardware is cited from roundup.cpp. The manifest also declares an inputs block (ports, actions, key bindings) that web/ reads to build its keyboard map — see porting — so a manifest without it can't be played in the browser.

Quickstart

Bring your own dkong.zip and you'll be playing in about a minute:

make rom-dkong     # assemble your ROM locally (sha256-checked)
make serve         # dev server (sets COOP/COEP), then open the printed URL

Pick Donkey Kong, press 5 to drop a coin and 1 to start — arrows or WASD to move, space to jump.

npm test           # the full unit suite (ROM-dependent ones skip cleanly if you haven't built one)

(make rom-dkong is an alias for make -C games/dkong rom; make serve is an alias for npm run serve — either form works, pick one.)

Requirements: Node, Python 3 (+ numpy, Pillow for the pixel gate), z80dasm (cross-checks the decoder for make verify), and — for regenerating MAME goldens — MAME 0.288 and ffmpeg.

Adding a game

See docs/README.md — the whole method — and docs/ for the technique guides. In short: pick (or write) the CPU and board, translate the ROM into games/<name>/, prove it pixel-exact against MAME, then decompile it to idiomatic JS and ground its mechanics by playing it under MAME.

License

GPLv3. The translation and tools are ours and free software; the original ROM data is not included and is not ours.

content_html_zh:
使用人工智能代理移植现有软件的实验。 该仓库中的反汇编、翻译、测试和工具均由代理完成。 Arcade ROM 是测试平台，选择它的原因之一是：您可以证明端口是否正确。

大多数移植工作没有预言机。 你重写一些东西，它看起来是正确的，而“忠实”仍然是一个观点问题。 街机 ROM 不存在这个问题 — MAME 已经运行它，因此有一个参考实现可以发出精确的预期输出。 正确性变得可证伪且逐帧：我们的 JavaScript 是否产生了与原始机器代码相同的像素，或者没有？

具体来说：街机游戏从原始机器代码转换为 JavaScript，并针对 MAME 进行了像素精确验证。 不是根据观察重新实现——ROM 被逐条指令地反汇编和翻译，然后逐帧检查，直到像素匹配。

可证伪的翻译是基础。 最重要的是，移植变得可读 - 例程被反编译为惯用的 JavaScript，每个例程都经过验证，相当于翻译的内存（对 The Pit 来说是完整的，对 Donkey Kong 来说也是如此） - 并且可以理解 - 游戏的机制是通过在 MAME 中玩游戏而建立的，而不是从代码中猜测出来的。 同一个预言机承担着双重职责：一个证明像素匹配的门，以及一个我们驱动来了解游戏含义的探测器。 整个方法只有一页：docs/README.md。

《大金刚》是第一个科目，而且已经完成。 Pit（Zilec/Centuri，1982）是第二个，它是经过深思熟虑选择的：不存在对其的公开反汇编，因此模型没有任何东西可以记住——特工必须从原始 ROM 中恢复它。 这使得它成为论文的更尖锐的测试，并且相同的可证伪像素门使其保持诚实。 该存储库的结构可以容纳许多内容：多个 CPU、多个街机板和多个游戏 romset，共享它们真正共享的内容。

代理是如何组织的——分工、我们实际遇到的故障模式以及工具必须对它们做什么——都写在 docs/how-the-agents-worked.md 中。

状态——大金刚：播放。 所有四块板、自然的板到板进展和关卡循环都可以工作 — 完成 100m 后，无限期地回绕到下一个关卡的 25m — 并且渲染是根据 MA​​ME 0.288 逐帧进行像素验证的。 状态 — The Pit：进行中。 它的整个启动→吸引序列运行并针对 MAME 进行像素精确渲染；它的所有 169 个例程现在都被重写为惯用的 JavaScript（内存相当于预言机，内存和例程根据证据命名，提议者≠确认者）；它的完整机制——目标、演员、赢/输——已经通过在 MAME 下玩来映射。 剩下的工作是端到端的游戏像素验证。

这里有什么（以及没有什么）

这个仓库包含了我们的工具、我们的翻译（JavaScript——我们自己对 ROM 逻辑的表达）和我们的理解——每个游戏的gameplay.md（它是如何玩的，来自公共研究）和 Mechanisms.md（它的工作原理的基于代码的模型）。 它不提供受版权保护的 ROM 数据，也不提供 gitignored 的构建元数据 — games/dkong/out/ 下的 dk.asm、coverage.json、blocks.def、unreached.txt（使用 make trace 在本地重新生成）。 您提供自己的 ROM； make rom-dkong 在本地进行组装和 sha256-验证。 请参阅 games/dkong/rom/README.md。

您仍然需要 ROM — 这就是原因

翻译取代了 ROM 的逻辑，而不是其内容。 ROM 不仅仅是代码：

  • 图形和调色板是纯数据。 gfx1（8×8 块）、gfx2（16×16 精灵）和颜色 proms 中根本没有代码。 没有它们就没有什么可画的。
  • 该代码将 ROM 作为数据读取。 大金刚的第一个游戏状态处理程序运行 ld hl,0x01ba / ldir，直接从 ROM 中复制表格。 因此，引擎仍然将 ROM 映射到地址空间并从中读取——我们的 JavaScript 是执行的，ROM 仍然是它读取的。

这正是版权线落入其中的原因：JavaScript 是我们自己的逻辑表达，并且它是发布的；原始数据是任天堂的，但从来没有。

我们如何知道这是正确的

如果问题是代理是否可以忠实地移植软件，那么答案的价值就在于可以证明它是错误的。 这些门是实验的仪器，每一个门都从干净的结账处运行：

大金刚的游戏开始介绍：左边是 MAME，右边是 arcade-js，由相同的输入磁带驱动，并与像素门自己的帧偏移对齐。 两个面板都是根据门差异的frames.rgb 工件渲染的，而不是两个窗口的屏幕记录。 以 2 倍速度显示；在这 35 秒的运行中，最大的单帧差异为 0.17%。

  • 像素门。 在固定的、确定性控制的命令行下从实时 MAME 0.288 捕获黄金，通过我们的引擎运行相同的输入磁带，并比较帧。 移动 6/6 和奖励项目 9/9 场景适用于所有四种棋盘类型。 这些场景会触发棋盘状态在给定的棋盘上开始，这使得每个场景都简短而确定——这是固定装置的属性，而不是游戏的限制，游戏会自行进展。
  • 解码器交叉检查。 我们的 Z80 解码器在整个 ROM 上与 z80dasm 进行检查：6051 指令边界，任一方向上的零分歧（进行验证）。
  • 步骤审核。 翻译中的每个 m.step() 目标都经过验证是否落在真实的指令边界上（进行步骤检查）。 静态跟踪器达到 ROM 的约 77%；未达到的跨度中的目标被报告为覆盖范围差距，而不是悄悄地算作通过——绿色的门表明了它实际覆盖的范围。
  • 数千个单元测试（npm 测试），在它们所证明的断言旁边记录了突变补丁，因此不会失败的测试本身就是可见的。 每个惯用的重写还带有针对冻结预言的内存等效性测试，它必须捕获故意破坏的双胞胎。
  • 陈述并写入差异。 RAM 和硬件写入表面的差异与像素无关，这将“CPU 转换错误”与“视频模型错误”区分开来。

布局

core/                 game-agnostic engine
  cpu/z80.js          the Z80 processor        (any Z80 game reuses this)
  cpu/test/           unit tests for the CPU core
  audio.js            sample-player abstraction (audio lives ABOVE emulation)
boards/               arcade hardware, named by MAME driver (a "board")
  dkong/              memory map · i8257/watchdog/latches · video/palette/geometry
  dkong/hardware.json the same, as JSON: the single source the shared Python gate
                      tools read via --hardware, instead of hardcoding DK addresses
  dkong/test/         unit tests for the board
games/                one directory per romset (dkong, thepit)
  dkong/
    manifest.js       declares its cpu + board + rom set + inputs + metadata
    translated/       the assembly-JS translation of the ROM (the frozen oracle)
    idiomatic/        readable-JS rewrites, each gated memory-equivalent to the oracle
    audio/            sound-command → sample trigger map
    rom/              gitignored — `make rom-dkong` builds it locally
    tapes/            test input tapes (published)
    test/             unit + integration tests for the translation
    entrypoints.json  disassembly entry points (folded into the trace)
    tools/            per-game gate runners (emit.js · move_suite.py · prize_suite.py)
  thepit/             the second game — same shape; its mechanisms.md maps the game
                      as understood so far (see docs/mechanisms)
web/                  browser front-end: pick a game and play it
tools/                disassembler · tracer · MAME golden capture · pixel/state diff ·
                       gate runner (verdict.sh) — shared, game-agnostic
docs/                 the method: one model (docs/README.md) + a technique guide per move

测试与它们测试的代码位于同一位置（core/**/test/、boards/**/test/、games/**/test/ — 请参阅 npm test 的 glob），而不是在单独的顶级 test/ 中。

这三层——CPU、主板、游戏——是独立的轴。 游戏的manifest.js将其CPU（z80）和主板（dkong）命名；机器组装CPU+主板+编译后的ROM。 例如，Frogger 将在未来的boards/galaxian/ 上重用 core/cpu/z80.js。 板根据其实现的 MAME 机器配置来命名 - 通常与驱动程序文件 (dkong) 相同，但并非总是如此：Pit 在 MAME 的 taito/roundup.cpp 系列文件中运行 thepit 配置，因此它位于boards/thepit/，而其硬件是从 roundup.cpp 引用的。 清单还声明了一个输入块（端口、操作、键绑定），web/ 读取该输入块来构建其键盘映射（请参阅移植），因此没有它的清单无法在浏览器中播放。

快速入门

带上你自己的 dkong.zip，大约一分钟后你就可以玩了：

make rom-dkong     # assemble your ROM locally (sha256-checked)
make serve         # dev server (sets COOP/COEP), then open the printed URL

选择大金刚，按 5 投下硬币，按 1 开始 - 箭头或 WASD 移动，空格跳跃。

npm test           # the full unit suite (ROM-dependent ones skip cleanly if you haven't built one)

（make rom-dkong 是 make -C games/dkong rom 的别名；makeserve 是 npm runserve 的别名——两种形式都可以，选择一个。）

要求：Node、Python 3（+ numpy、用于像素门的 Pillow）、z80dasm（交叉检查解码器以进行验证）以及 — 用于重新生成 MAME 黄金 — MAME 0.288 和 ffmpeg。

添加游戏

请参阅 docs/README.md — 整个方法 — 和 docs/ 了解技术指南。 简而言之：选择（或编写）CPU 和主板，将 ROM 转换为 games/<name>/，针对 MAME 证明其像素精确，然后将其反编译为惯用的 JS，并通过在 MAME 下运行来磨练其机制。
